messages:
Maya R: Quick update — ran a small onboard smoke for orchid-10b v1.0 (chat + long-form summarization). Int6 and Int4 runs finished. Posting highlights and a short recs list.

Jon P: nice, numbers?

Maya R: TL;DR: int4 reduces decode cost ~2.9x vs fp16, int6 ~1.8x. Quality drop on long-form summarization: int4 ~3.6% ROUGE-L relative, int6 ~1.3%. Latency tail: int4 p95 +18ms, int6 +7ms on our 80-token median workloads.

Sara L: can you paste the unit econ so product can evaluate tradeoff?

Maya R: sure — quick calc we used: cost_per_1k_tokens_fp16 = $0.22, int6 = $0.12, int4 = $0.075. So cost multiplier vs fp16 = [1.0, 0.545, 0.341]. Saved per 1M tokens: int6 ~$110, int4 ~$145. (rough numbers, infra pricing baked in)

Derek C: interesting. What's the quality impact for short prompts / chat-like flows?

Maya R: for chat (<=64 tokens) BLEU/ROUGE differences are <1% vs fp16 for int6, and ~1.8% for int4. The big hit is in long-context retrieval summaries and very factual numeric extraction tasks.

Jon P: any regressions that would be visible in GTN or flagged by our evals?

Maya R: we ran the GTN smoke set (1k examples): int6 passes all redline metrics, int4 fails 2 of the product-critical slices (date/number fidelity and multi-step extraction). Failing examples attached in the sheet.

Sara L: link?

Maya R: https://docs.internal/redwood/onboard/orchid-10b/smoke-1713009999.xlsx

ops-bot: deployment-checker: canary pool available (5 GPUs), current queued jobs: 3.

Derek C: From a product risk POV I’d prefer int6 as default for chat features and route a low-cost int4 path for non-sensitive batch jobs (embeddings, summarization drafts) behind an explicit flag.

Jon P: +1 to Derek. Also suggest an A/B with fallback: start int6 default, measure GTN metric delta over 2 weeks, fallback to fp16 if delta > threshold. Do we have a threshold?

Maya R: propose threshold = 2% absolute drop on core GTN quality score for critical slices OR any failure on the numeric/date fidelity slice. If triggered, auto rollback to fp16 in the canary region.

Sara L: product asks for a crisp recommendation for sales/GTN: 1) Chat endpoints: recommend int6 default, fp16 opt-in for highest fidelity customers; 2) Batch/non-interactive: int4 allowed behind a quality opt-out; 3) Offer a "cost-savings" toggle in console showing estimated monthly $ savings and likely quality impact.

Jon P: add a note: for bursty workloads we need to validate int4 kvcache memory behavior — saw occasional +5% OOMs in one run.

Maya R: noted — will run memory sweep and add to the ops checklist. Suggested next steps: short-run A/B on 5% traffic int6 vs fp16 for chat; separate batch pilot for int4 with automated GTN gating; update the scorecard and product-facing blurb.

Derek C: sounds good. If you push the A/B plan, I’ll prep the customer-facing wording and the console toggle UX draft.

Sara L: I’ll update the onboard scorecard and attach the failing example picks so GTN PM can vet.

Maya R: thanks — will create tickets and tag you all. ping me if you want raw logs (I have the diff dumps and the seed examples).

Jon P: thanks — appreciate the quick scan. :thumbsup:
